[[File:Forfeit Zero 2003-05-25 Ignoble Origins.gif|thumb|right|300px|"Ignoble Origins", the first ''Forfeit Zero'' strip. Ben and Ethus explain the comic's mission.]]
'''''Forfeit Zero''''' was a webcomic about the ''Star Wars Customizable Card Game'' written and "drawn" by [[Brian Sabotta]], who posted as '''ben_ethus'''. It ran from May 2003 to November 2005, mostly on a Monday, Wednesday and Friday schedule. Its stick-figure cast of card players carried on a running feud with the "fiendish" [[Players Committee]], and its readers gathered on [[Game Players Network]] and [[DeckTech]]. The complete run of strips and news posts is preserved at the '''Forfeit Zero Archive''', [https://comic.forfeitzero.com/ comic.forfeitzero.com].<ref name="archive">[https://comic.forfeitzero.com/ Forfeit Zero Archive], comic.forfeitzero.com. Every strip carries the credit "Written and 'Drawn' by Brian Sabotta"; every news post is signed "-ben_ethus" above the footer "Forfeit Zero - Created by Brian Sabotta". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101200206/https://comic.forfeitzero.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>

The title is SWCCG jargon: a card with forfeit 0 does nothing to absorb battle damage. In "Establishing the Establishment", Newbie loses his "forfeit zero dude" and the overflow kills him.<ref name="s20030722">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030722.html "Establishing the Establishment"], ''Forfeit Zero'' strip (22 July 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102075522/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030722.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== History ==

=== Origins (2003) ===
Sabotta unveiled the comic in a Game Players Network forum thread he started under the heading "Diversions from Deckbuilding". He later called GPN the "sort-of official" ''Forfeit Zero'' message board and credited its regulars with "more comics/punchlines than you're probably aware".<ref name="p20040121">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040121.html "Artists Steal"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (21 January 2004). "Never really imagined that after posting my first 'Diversions from Deckbuilding' post that over 80 comics would come as a result."</ref><ref name="p20031114">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031114.html "Bootlegs"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (14 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102080642/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031114.html Internet Archive]</ref> The first strip, "Ignoble Origins", introduces Ben and Ethus, whose "mission" is "to amuse you using pictures and words on the subject of our favoritest card game: Star Wars: CCG! Or, failing that, to pointlessly belittle you".<ref name="s20030525">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030525.html "Ignoble Origins"], ''Forfeit Zero'' strip (25 May 2003).</ref> Its footer gives the comic's first address, home.earthlink.net/ben_ethus/forfeitzero. By July the strips pointed to forfeitzero.keenspace.com, a free host.<ref name="s20030525" /><ref name="s20030722" />

On 22 July 2003 Sabotta set out the comic's direction. He said he was "a fan of the Player's Committee" and liked "what they're doing to promote and maintain a game that is, technically, dead". The PC debate on the forums still gave him the springboard for "the next major plotline".<ref name="p20030722">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030722.html "Cheeky Tongues"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (22 July 2003). "This next run of comics will serve as the springboard to launch into the next major plotline" Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102075522/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030722.html Internet Archive]</ref> He meant to post on Tuesdays and Thursdays but settled into Monday, Wednesday and Friday.<ref name="p20031010">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031010.html "Daddy Longlegger"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (10 October 2003). "I update this crazy page with a new comic every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday." Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102080241/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031010.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20040303">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040303.html "Celebrate Good Times, Come On!"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (3 March 2004).</ref>

=== Growing readership ===
The 50th strip went up on 3 November 2003, the 75th on 31 December 2003 and the 100th on 3 March 2004.<ref name="p20031103">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031103.html "Number 50!"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (3 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101205737/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031103.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20040102">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040102.html "Happy New Year!"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (2 January 2004). "As an aside, Wednesday's comic was #75!" Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101210418/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040102.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20040303" /> Site visits nearly doubled from 554 in September 2003 to 1,066 in November.<ref name="p20031203">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031203.html "Har Har"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (3 December 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101210335/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031203.html Internet Archive]</ref> Readers wrote in from Mexico, and the site's statistics showed visitors from Germany and Yugoslavia. A reader, Rodrigo Hernández, volunteered to translate the archive into Spanish. Translated strips appeared from December 2003, and they got their own pages in January 2004.<ref name="p20031022">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031022.html "Unfair Advantage"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (22 October 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102080357/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031022.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20031210">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031210.html "Worldly Humor"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (10 December 2003).</ref><ref name="p20031217">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031217.html "Out-of-Date Topical Humor#2"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (17 December 2003).</ref><ref name="p20040109">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040109.html "Actualy Updated Something"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (9 January 2004).</ref> Outages at its free host repeatedly knocked the site offline, and in early February 2004 the comic's auto-updater broke.<ref name="p20031001">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031001.html "Mileage May Vary"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (1 October 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101204946/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031001.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20040204">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040204.html "Site Sorta Fixed"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (4 February 2004).</ref><ref name="p20040215">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040215.html "'Free' Hosting"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (15 February 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101211659/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040215.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== The 100th-comic contest ===
To mark the 100th strip, Sabotta asked readers to email their "favoritest" ''Forfeit Zero'' comic and say why. The prize was a character based on the winner, with the winner choosing the name "and (most importantly) ... the hat".<ref name="p20040303" /> He could not choose between two entries, so on 19 March 2004 he named two winners. [[Rustan Sharer]] ("Rogue 4") picked "Exchange Rate" (22 October 2003) and became '''Ned''', a lost explorer in a pith helmet. [[David Destefanis]] ("DDM") picked "Brainiac" and became '''David De Master''', who wears a Napoleonic bicorne and plots "First Locals, then European Championships, then the WORLD!!!!".<ref name="p20040319">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040319.html "Double Your Pleasure"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (19 March 2004).</ref><ref name="s20040319">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040319.html "New Faces"], ''Forfeit Zero'' strip (19 March 2004).</ref>

=== Slowdown and the WARS years (2004–2005) ===
From late March 2004 updates thinned out. Sabotta was busy with his personal life and then with a new job as a computer programmer in Pittsburgh. He promised "I won't let the comic die".<ref name="p20040330">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040330.html "Hey Guys..."], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (30 March 2004). "Rest assured, I won't let the comic die."</ref><ref name="p20040607">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040607.html "New Career Goals"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (7 June 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101212523/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040607.html Internet Archive]</ref> Through 2004 many strips turned to Decipher's new ''[[WARS TCG]]''. He explained that "the success/failure of Wars could have a significant impact on the future of SW:CCG", and he expected Virtual Set 7 to bring the comic back to SWCCG.<ref name="p20040711">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040711.html "Everyone's A Critic"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (11 July 2004).</ref> He wrote the "Email of the Week" read on ''Wars Radio'' in September 2004.<ref name="p20040927">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040927.html "Still Riding My 15 Minutes...?"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (27 September 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101212943/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040927.html Internet Archive]</ref> When [[Mark Tuttle]] came to Pittsburgh on the Decipher Wars Tour that November, Sabotta lost to him and gave him a ''Forfeit Zero'' "L.O.B. Sandwich" T-shirt from the comic's new online store.<ref name="p20041110">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20041110.html "So, Yeah..."], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (10 November 2004).</ref> A January 2005 series, "Two Weeks Ago", attacked what he called Decipher's "poor decision making", and "Firstage" (29 January 2005) was a "pseudo-SWCCG comic" from an author who admitted he hadn't played the game "in ages".<ref name="p20050105">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20050105.html "*grumble*"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (5 January 2005).</ref><ref name="p20050129">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20050129.html "Roots"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (29 January 2005).</ref>

=== Skiffit and the last strips ===
After almost no strips over the summer of 2005, Sabotta explained in October that he and two friends had been building Skiffit.com. The site let collectors buy and sell Star Wars CCG cards, video games and other trading cards at fixed prices instead of by auction. He said ''Forfeit Zero'' would move there from "lame Keenspace with their frequent service outages and annoying banner ad".<ref name="p20051018">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20051018.html "Big Announcement!"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (18 October 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102140502/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20051018.html Internet Archive]</ref> He listed his own spare SWCCG cards for sale on the new site. The last news post, "Skiffit Lives!", went up with the strip "It Talks" on 2 November 2005.<ref name="p20051102">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20051102.html "Skiffit Lives!"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (2 November 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101213739/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20051102.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Rediscovery and the new archive (2023–2026) ===
On 24 March 2023 the forum user quickdraw3457 started a "Forfeit Zero Comic" thread on the Players Committee forums. He posted that the comic was still online at forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com, its old Keenspace address, "in all its original glory". He added that Brian "might try to host it himself", was "pretty flattered that people still remember it" and was "shocked that the original host was still live".<ref name="fz2023">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1402333#p1402333 Forfeit Zero Comic], quickdraw3457, forum.starwarsccg.org (24–25 March 2023). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101200153/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t82626.html Internet Archive].</ref> Throdo asked how he had not heard of it in "the last 16 years I've been back in the game". quickdraw3457 replied that it "had kind of faded away by 2007ish".<ref name="fz2023b">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1404027#p1404027 Forfeit Zero Comic], Throdo and quickdraw3457, forum.starwarsccg.org (19 April 2023). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101200153/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t82626.html Internet Archive].</ref>

On 1 November 2026 Sabotta, posting as ben ethus, announced the comic's "new permanent home" at comic.forfeitzero.com. The archive shows each original strip with its news post, if one existed, and navigates by file name. He said this is "mostly chronological, but has a few oddities due to files that got renamed". He also explained the rabbit: "Over 20 years ago, someone got all bent out of shape about one of the comics, so I had redacted it with a placeholder." He wrote that it was still amazing to him "that 1) anyone remembers it or 2) anyone could possibly still care about it", and called the comic "the one contribution to the hobby I was able to make aside from getting obliterated in every tournament I ever played in".<ref name="fz2026">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1451112#p1451112 Forfeit Zero Comic], ben ethus (Brian Sabotta), forum.starwarsccg.org (1 November 2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101200153/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t82626.html Internet Archive].</ref> [[Scott Lingrell]] replied "Awesome! Thanks for posting this!"<ref name="fz2026b">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1451114#p1451114 Forfeit Zero Comic], Advocate (Scott Lingrell), forum.starwarsccg.org (1 November 2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101200153/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t82626.html Internet Archive].</ref>

=== Websites ===
The comic had three homes.<ref name="s20030525" /><ref name="s20030722" />
* '''home.earthlink.net/ben_ethus/forfeitzero''' – the address printed on the first strip in May 2003.
* '''forfeitzero.keenspace.com''' – the free Keenspace webcomic host, from July 2003. The same site still answers at '''[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/ forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com]'''. It keeps features the new archive does not have: a page for each strip with its news post, a calendar archive ("Raiders of the Lost Archive"), the "Roll Call" character page, a links page, and six Spanish translations of strips from 25–29 May 2003 and 10 December 2003. It also has the 19 April 2004 "Guest Strip" (made for ''Real Life Comics''), which is missing from the new archive.<ref name="cgsite">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/ Forfeit Zero], forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com (the original Keenspace site): [http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/archive.html archive], [http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/characters.html Roll Call], [http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/links.html links], [http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/20030525esp.html Spanish edition], [http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040419.html 19 April 2004].</ref><ref name="p20040419">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040419.html "Submitted to Mr. Dean"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (19 April 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101213219/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040419.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''[https://comic.forfeitzero.com/ comic.forfeitzero.com]''' – the "new permanent home" Sabotta opened in November 2026. It shows each strip with its news post and navigates by file name.<ref name="fz2026" />

== Story and characters ==
[[File:Forfeit Zero 2003-07-22 Establishing the Establishment.gif|thumb|right|300px|"Establishing the Establishment" (22 July 2003) introduced the Players Committee Headquarters, a castle on a hill.]]
The strips are stick figures with round heads, black faces and hats. Sabotta noted that the "action" was "a bunch of sticks and circles sitting around talking", and he added colour only for outdoor scenes.<ref name="p20030924">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030924.html "Murphy"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (24 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101205212/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030924.html Internet Archive]</ref> The site's "Roll Call" page introduced the cast with parody cards and short bios. Most are mock ''Star Wars'' CCG cards; Shádow 839 is drawn as a ''Lord of the Rings TCG'' card and Chibi as a Pokémon card.<ref name="rollcall">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/characters.html Forfeit Zero: Roll Call], forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com (character cards and bios by Brian Sabotta). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102140645/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/characters.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20031208">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031208.html "Wonder of Wonders"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (8 December 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102080811/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031208.html Internet Archive]</ref>

* '''Ben''' ("Card Game Enthusiast") – "more or less your average run-of-the-mill Star Wars:CCG player. (Even if he is just an eyeball with arms and legs.)" He plays mainly for fun and is "best-friends/arch-nemesis" with Ethus. Both have played since the game was first released.<ref name="rollcall" />
* '''Ethus''' ("Collectible Card Gamer") – raised on a farm he hates. He is "forever chewing on a piece of hay" and "never without his straw hat". Together the two names make Sabotta's handle, ben_ethus.<ref name="rollcall" /><ref name="s20030525" />
* '''The Newbie''' ("Gaming Neophyte"; also "Newb", "Newbo") – just introduced to SWCCG. He wears a pointed cap marked "N", and his first deck "blows".<ref name="rollcall" /><ref name="s20030722" />
* '''Shádow 839''' ("Enforcer of the Committee") – "Dark minion of the dreaded Player's Committee", who makes sure players obey the Committee's leader: "For your sake, I hope you play 'Virtual Cards.'"<ref name="rollcall" />
* '''Chibi''' and '''Larry Potter''' – the "dire fiends" of the license quest. Chibi is a furry creature who plays Wizards of the Coast's ''Star Wars Trading Card Game'' and "hates Yahtzee". Larry, "the semi-retarded, bastard cousin of a prominent literary figure", hangs out with Chibi, "who despises him".<ref name="rollcall" /><ref name="s20040218" />
* '''Uncle Dan''' ("Gamer Mechanic") – "quite possibly the only mechanic to ever play the game of Star Wars:CCG".<ref name="rollcall" />
* '''The Boss''' – owns the shop where Ben, Ethus and Newbie work. He hired them after Ethus beat him at SWCCG, even though he was using his 1996 Regional Championship decks.<ref name="rollcall" />
* '''L.O.B. Sandwich''' – Ethus's left-over bologna sandwich and "resident SW:CCG expert at Bob's Deli", who beat Newbie in a tournament game. A ''Forfeit Zero'' T-shirt carried his picture.<ref name="rollcall" /><ref name="p20041110" />
* '''Sam''' – a girl who plays Star Wars, introduced at a card sale in "Rarity" (20 October 2003). '''Gary''' and '''Fez Man''' are other recurring friends.<ref name="s20031020">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031020.html "Rarity"], ''Forfeit Zero'' strip (20 October 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101205851/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031020.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20040303" />
* '''Ned''' and '''David De Master''' – the contest winners' characters (2004).<ref name="p20040319" />
* A yellow board-game pawn who lures Ben away from card games in July 2005 ("A New Face").<ref name="s20050705">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20050705.html "A New Face"], ''Forfeit Zero'' strip (5 July 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101213630/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20050705.html Internet Archive]</ref>

The main plot began in July 2003. A Player's Committee hidden in its fortress learns that a newbie is "''not'' using our Virtual Cards" and resolves "to put a stop to this". The strip explains that when Decipher lost the license, "a group of players banded together to take control of the game, and called themselves the 'Player's Committee' ... unleashing free new cards, rules updates, and tournament prizes upon the unsuspecting masses". Newbie answers by vowing to take the Committee head on, "seize the Star Wars license by force and return it to Decipher".<ref name="s20030827">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030827.html "Dire Fiends"], ''Forfeit Zero'' strip (27 August 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102075432/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030827.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="s20030905">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030905.html "Epic Plans Commence"], ''Forfeit Zero'' strip (5 September 2003).</ref> Sabotta hoped "the friendly folks who run the Player's Committee have a sense of humor" and asked the same of the Shadow Squadron.<ref name="p20030827">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030827.html "PC Humor"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (27 August 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102075432/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030827.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20030829">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030829.html "More PC Humor"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (29 August 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102075536/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030829.html Internet Archive]</ref> The quest led the trio to the "dire fiends holding the Star Wars merchandising license hostage". These turned out to be Wizards of the Coast's ''Star Wars TCG'' players. In February 2004 the story resumed as the "ongoing adventures of Ben & Ethus & The Newb in their quest to get the license back from WotC to foil the fiendish PC".<ref name="s20031208">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031208.html "Realization"], ''Forfeit Zero'' strip (8 December 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102080811/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031208.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="s20040218">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040218.html "Trailer"], ''Forfeit Zero'' strip (18 February 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101211623/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040218.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20040218">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040218.html "Coming Soon!"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (18 February 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101211623/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040218.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Topics ==
Between story arcs the comic followed the SWCCG news of its day:
* '''Virtual cards.''' In September 2003 Sabotta followed the PC's polls for the first player-created virtual cards of [[Virtual Set 6: City In The Clouds|Virtual Set 6]]. He backed "Why Didn't You Tell Me?" for the Dark Side card and correctly predicted "Brief Loss of Control" and "Impressive, Most Impressive" as the winners.<ref name="p20030903">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030903.html "Cross Reference"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (3 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102202837/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030903.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20030905">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030905.html "Ta-Daaaa!"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (5 September 2003).</ref><ref name="p20030910">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030910.html "No "We" In Team"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (10 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102080226/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030910.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20030912">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030912.html "I'm So Very Sorry"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (12 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101205051/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030912.html Internet Archive]</ref> He made Virtual Set 6 strips in December 2003 ("Out-of-Date Topical Humor") and won games with [[Civil Disorder (V) (Virtual Set 6: City In The Clouds)|Civil Disorder (V)]] and [[Boba Fett's Blaster Rifle (V) (Virtual Set 6: City In The Clouds)|Boba Fett's Blaster Rifle (V)]].<ref name="p20031214">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031214.html "Out-of-Date Topical Humor"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (14 December 2003).</ref><ref name="p20031124">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031124.html "Fifty-Fifty"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (24 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102080824/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031124.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20031222">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031222.html "Tourney Results!"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (22 December 2003).</ref> A January 2004 strip about "the latest Virtual Card set" set off "a fierce debate" on the GPN boards.<ref name="p20040119">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040119.html "Finally"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (19 January 2004).</ref>
* '''Decipher.''' A long 24 October 2003 post attacked Decipher's new sanctioned-tournament system for turning "Tournament Directors into Marketing Shills". It praised the players who had kept "a game that has officially been out-of-print for the past few years alive through sheer determination".<ref name="p20031024">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031024.html "Righteous Indignation"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (24 October 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102080412/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031024.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''DeckTech and GPN.''' Sabotta joined [[DeckTech]] in October 2003, and his Ewok deck "Bad News Bears" reached #5 on its Top 10 SWCCG list. A February 2004 strip answered players who complained that DeckTech was past its prime.<ref name="p20031022" /><ref name="p20040206">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040206.html "Ask Not What DeckTech Can Do For You, But..."], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (6 February 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101211516/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040206.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Local tournaments.''' News posts carried tournament reports from the Pittsburgh scene: Helm's Deep, Dormont and an unsanctioned event at a Boston Market after a card shop event gave way to Pokémon players. Several reports became strips, such as "Scenes From Yesterday's Tourney" from the 20 December 2003 Dormont tournament.<ref name="p20030929">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030929.html "Good News"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (29 September 2003). "Star Wars canceled to make way for Pokemon. How typical." Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261102075802/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030929.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20031006">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031006.html "Ritualistic Beating"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (6 October 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101205646/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20031006.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20031222" /><ref name="p20040107">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040107.html "Sad, But True"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (7 January 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101213125/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20040107.html Internet Archive]</ref> His regular opponent was his friend [[Shewski]].<ref name="p20030915">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030915.html "Temptation"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (15 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101205102/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030915.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20031208" />
* '''Other games.''' Strips poked fun at ''Magic: The Gathering'', ''Yu-Gi-Oh!'', Wizards of the Coast's ''Star Wars TCG'' and later WARS. The September 2003 "Off-Topic" strip, about a Chuck Palahniuk talk, was soon replaced by a rabbit placeholder, "FLUFFY BUNNY!!!". Sabotta linked the original for readers who "don't get offended easily". In 2026 he explained that "someone got all bent out of shape" about it.<ref name="p20030917">[http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030917.html "True Story (Alternate Image)"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (17 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101205116/http://forfeitzero.comicgenesis.com/d/20030917.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="p20040711" /><ref name="fz2026" />

== Strips ==
There are 145 dated strips and one alternate, listed in date order with a short summary of each. Titles are taken from each strip's header. Each link opens the strip's page on the original site, with its news post.<ref name="archive" /><ref name="cgsite" />
